notes: cta B : avant/après, sur une image sans visage, slide 5. essai (numéro en 0). Schéma stop-doing, jamais fait chez nous, au plus près du gagnant (« as a married man », 266 k vues le 23/10). Accroches écrites : « Things you should stop doing as a boyfriend » (retenue : le gagnant transposé à notre public plus jeune), « Things you should stop doing in a relationship » (écartée : plus vague), « Stop doing this if you want her to stay » (écartée : ton de manipulation). Angle respectueux : attention, effort, communication. Items neufs, sans reprendre ceux du gagnant (tâches, affection, sentiments, défense).

slides.texte_overlay:
Things you should stop doing
as a boyfriend

Stop picking up your phone while she's talking. Put it face down, or better, in your pocket. Nothing on that screen matters more than the person sitting right in front of you telling you about her day.
Stop making her plan every date. Pick the place, book the table, figure out the evening. "I've got Saturday covered." It's not about money. It's about showing you actually thought about it.
Stop going silent when something bothers you. Sulking for two days helps nobody. Say it calmly. "Hey, that thing earlier kind of got to me. Can we talk?" Clear beats moody every time.
Stop running out of things to talk about at dinner. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you've always got something new to share. Couples who keep learning never get boring together.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: the same three topics at every dinner. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app, and there's always something new to share. History, art, science. Never boring.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop forgetting the things she told you. Her exam on Thursday, her friend's drama, the song she loves. Remembering small details is how she knows you're actually listening, not just nodding.
Stop competing with her friends. Get to know them, ask about them, be easy to have around. A guy her friends like is a guy she never has to defend, and that makes everything easier for both of you.
Stop thinking the effort ends once she's yours. Keep asking her out, keep the small surprises, keep saying thank you. The effort that got her there is the same effort that keeps her happy.
